### `bb repo admin create`

Create a new repository

```text
bb repo admin create [flags]
```

Alias for bb repo create.

```bash
# Create a repository in a project
bb repo admin create --project PROJ --name billing-service

# With a description and a default branch
bb repo admin create --project PROJ --name billing-service \
  --description "Billing API" --default-branch main
```

`--default-branch string`
:   Repository default branch

`--description string`
:   Repository description

`--forkable`
:   Repository forkable (default true)

`--name string`
:   Repository name

`--project string`
:   Project key

Inherited from [`bb repo admin`](#bb-repo-admin):

`--repo string`
:   Repository as PROJECT/slug (defaults to the repository of the git checkout you are in, then BITBUCKET\_PROJECT\_KEY + BITBUCKET\_REPO\_SLUG)

Also takes the [global flags](global-flags.md).

### `bb repo admin delete`

Delete a repository

```text
bb repo admin delete [PROJECT/slug] [flags]
```

Alias for bb repo delete.

```bash
# Delete a repository; at a terminal bb asks first
bb repo admin delete PROJ/repo

# In a script, where nobody can be asked; --yes counts only when the repository is named
bb repo admin delete PROJ/repo --yes
```

`--yes`
:   Skip the confirmation. Only applies when the repository is named explicitly.

## `bb repo archive`

Download repository archive

```text
bb repo archive [flags]
```

```bash
# Download the repository as repo.zip
bb repo archive --repo PROJ/repo

# One directory of a tagged release, as a tarball
bb repo archive --repo PROJ/repo --at v1.2.0 --path docs --format tar.gz \
  --output docs-1.2.0.tar.gz
```

`--at string`
:   The commit to stream an archive of

`--format string`
:   The format to stream the archive in (one of: zip, tar, tar.gz, tgz) (default "zip")

`-o, --output string`
:   Output filename (use '-' for stdout, defaults to &lt;repo-slug&gt;.&lt;format&gt;)

`--path string`
:   Paths to include in the streamed archive

`--prefix string`
:   A prefix to apply to all entries in the streamed archive

`--repo string`
:   Repository as PROJECT/slug (defaults to the repository of the git checkout you are in, then BITBUCKET\_PROJECT\_KEY + BITBUCKET\_REPO\_SLUG)

Also takes the [global flags](global-flags.md).

**Dry run:** Runs as usual: this command changes nothing, so there is nothing to hold back

### `bb repo browse raw`

Get raw file content

```text
bb repo browse raw <path> [flags]
```

The file is written to stdout as it arrives, byte for byte, whatever its size. With --json it is returned inside the document instead -- as text, or as base64 when it is not text -- which holds it in memory, so a file larger than 64 MiB is refused under --json.

```bash
# A file's bytes, saved locally
bb repo browse raw docs/logo.png --repo PROJ/repo > logo.png
```

`--at string`
:   Commit ID or ref

Inherited from [`bb repo browse`](#bb-repo-browse):

`--repo string`
:   Repository as PROJECT/slug (defaults to the repository of the git checkout you are in, then BITBUCKET\_PROJECT\_KEY + BITBUCKET\_REPO\_SLUG)

Also takes the [global flags](global-flags.md).

**Dry run:** Runs as usual: this command changes nothing, so there is nothing to hold back

## `bb repo cat`

Output the raw content of a file over REST

```text
bb repo cat <path> [flags]
```

The file is written to stdout as it arrives, byte for byte, whatever its size. With --json it is returned inside the document instead -- as text, or as base64 when it is not text -- which holds it in memory, so a file larger than 64 MiB is refused under --json.

```bash
# Print a file without cloning the repository
bb repo cat README.md --repo PROJ/repo

# As it was at a tag
bb repo cat README.md --repo PROJ/repo --at v1.2.0
```

`--at string`
:   Commit ID or ref to cat

`--repo string`
:   Repository as PROJECT/slug (defaults to the repository of the git checkout you are in, then BITBUCKET\_PROJECT\_KEY + BITBUCKET\_REPO\_SLUG)

## `bb repo clone`

Clone a repository to the local filesystem

```text
bb repo clone <repository> [directory] [-- <gitflags>...] [flags]
```

Also available as bb clone.

```bash
# Clone into a directory named after the repository
bb repo clone PROJ/repo

# By the address the browser shows, into a directory of your choice
bb repo clone https://bitbucket.example.com/projects/PROJ/repos/repo work/repo

# Over HTTPS only, passing flags on to git
bb repo clone PROJ/repo --https -- --depth 1
```

`--https`
:   Use HTTPS only and skip the SSH clone attempt

`--no-upstream`
:   Do not add an upstream remote when cloning a fork

`--ssh`
:   Use SSH only and disable HTTPS fallback

`-u, --upstream-remote-name string`
:   Upstream remote name when cloning a fork (default "upstream")

Also takes the [global flags](global-flags.md).

**Dry run:** Shows that it would clone into a new directory, without doing it; nothing is checked first (predicted)

    projectKey     string   Project key the repository belongs to.

## `bb repo comment`

Add, list, update and delete comments on commits and pull requests

[`create`](#bb-repo-comment-create)
:   Create a comment

[`delete`](#bb-repo-comment-delete)
:   Delete a comment

[`list`](#bb-repo-comment-list)
:   List comments

[`update`](#bb-repo-comment-update)
:   Update a comment

### `bb repo comment create`

Create a comment

```text
bb repo comment create [flags]
```

Create a comment on a commit or a pull request.

Pass --parent to reply to an existing comment rather than start a new thread. The id to pass is the one `bb repo comment list` reports; a reply carries reply and parentId in that listing, so a thread can be walked back to its root.

```bash
# Comment on a line of a file in a commit
bb repo comment create --commit a1b2c3d --repo PROJ/repo \
  --path src/main.go --line 41 --text "This swallows the error."

# Reply to a comment on a pull request
bb repo comment create --pr 42 --repo PROJ/repo --parent 1389396 --text "Fixed."
```

`--line int`
:   Line within --path to anchor the comment to

`--line-type string`
:   Which side of the diff --line refers to (one of: ADDED, REMOVED, CONTEXT)

`--parent int`
:   Reply to this comment id instead of starting a new thread

`--path string`
:   Anchor the comment to this file, which is what makes it listable

`--text string`
:   Comment text

Inherited from [`bb repo comment`](#bb-repo-comment):

`--commit string`
:   Commit ID context

`--pr string`
:   Pull request ID context

`--repo string`
:   Repository as PROJECT/slug (defaults to the repository of the git checkout you are in, then BITBUCKET\_PROJECT\_KEY + BITBUCKET\_REPO\_SLUG)

Also takes the [global flags](global-flags.md).

**Dry run:** Predicts the outcome from what it can read, without changing anything (predicted)

### `bb repo comment delete`


## `bb repo compare`

Compare commits or branches

```text
bb repo compare <from> <to> [flags]
```

Compare commits or branches: what is reachable from &lt;from&gt; but not from &lt;to&gt;. Pass the ref you are asking about first; git log's range puts it last.

```text
bb repo compare feature/x main        # what feature/x adds
bb repo compare main feature/x        # nothing, unless main has moved
```

```bash
# The commits feature/x adds to main
bb repo compare feature/x main --repo PROJ/repo

# As a diff
bb repo compare feature/x main --repo PROJ/repo --diff
```

`--diff`
:   Show the unified diff of the changes

`--repo string`
:   Repository as PROJECT/slug (defaults to the repository of the git checkout you are in, then BITBUCKET\_PROJECT\_KEY + BITBUCKET\_REPO\_SLUG)

Also takes the [global flags](global-flags.md).

**Dry run:** Runs as usual: this command changes nothing, so there is nothing to hold back

<details class="note" data-search-exclude>
<summary>Output with <code>--json</code>, where <code>?</code> marks a field that can be absent</summary>
<pre><code>data
  repository     object
    projectKey   string                  Project key the repository belongs to.
    slug         string                  Repository slug.
  from           string                  Ref the comparison started at.
  to             string                  Ref it ended at.
  changes        list of object or null  Files that differ between the two.
    path         string                  Path after the change.
    srcPath?     string                  Path before a rename or copy.
    type?        string                  ADD, MODIFY, DELETE, COPY, MOVE or UNKNOWN.
    nodeType?    string                  FILE, DIRECTORY or SUBMODULE.
    executable?  boolean                 Whether the file is executable after the change.
  patch?         string                  The unified diff, when --diff was passed.
</code></pre>
</details>

## `bb repo default-task`

Add, list, update and delete the tasks each pull request in a repository starts with

[`add`](#bb-repo-default-task-add)
:   Add a default checklist task

[`delete`](#bb-repo-default-task-delete)
:   Delete a default checklist task

[`list`](#bb-repo-default-task-list)
:   List default checklist tasks

[`update`](#bb-repo-default-task-update)
:   Update a default checklist task

### `bb repo default-task add`

Add a default checklist task

```text
bb repo default-task add <description> [flags]
```

```bash
# A task every new pull request in the repository starts with
bb repo default-task add "Update the changelog" --repo PROJ/repo

# Only for pull requests from a feature branch into main
bb repo default-task add "Update the changelog" --repo PROJ/repo \
  --source-ref 'feature/*' --target-ref main
```

`--source-ref string`
:   Source ref to match; a glob matches as a pattern, anything else as a branch (default: any ref)

`--target-ref string`
:   Target ref to match; a glob matches as a pattern, anything else as a branch (default: any ref)

Inherited from [`bb repo default-task`](#bb-repo-default-task):

`--repo string`
:   Repository as PROJECT/slug (defaults to the repository of the git checkout you are in, then BITBUCKET\_PROJECT\_KEY + BITBUCKET\_REPO\_SLUG)

Also takes the [global flags](global-flags.md).

## `bb repo delete`

Delete a repository

```text
bb repo delete [PROJECT/slug] [flags]
```

Name the repository as a PROJECT/slug argument or with --repo. Without one it is inferred from the git remote, and --yes does not apply to an inferred target: a safety flag that works on a target you did not name is not one. At a terminal the confirmation names what will be deleted.

Also available as bb repo admin delete.

```bash
# Delete a repository; at a terminal bb asks first
bb repo delete PROJ/repo

# In a script, where nobody can be asked; --yes counts only when the repository is named
bb repo delete PROJ/repo --yes
```

`--repo string`
:   Repository as PROJECT/slug (defaults to the repository of the git checkout you are in, then BITBUCKET\_PROJECT\_KEY + BITBUCKET\_REPO\_SLUG)

`--yes`
:   Skip the confirmation. Only applies when the repository is named explicitly.

Also takes the [global flags](global-flags.md).

## `bb repo edit`

Edit a file's content over REST

```text
bb repo edit <path> [flags]
```

```bash
# Change a file on a branch in one commit, naming the commit you read it at
bb repo edit VERSION --repo PROJ/repo --branch main --source-commit a1b2c3d \
  --content "1.2.1" --message "Bump the version to 1.2.1"

# Add a file on a new branch cut from main, with its content from stdin
bb repo edit docs/notes.md --repo PROJ/repo --branch feature/notes \
  --source-branch main --content - --message "Add notes" < notes.md
```

`--branch string`
:   The branch on which the file should be modified or created

`--content string`
:   The full content of the file

`--message string`
:   Commit message

`--repo string`
:   Repository as PROJECT/slug (defaults to the repository of the git checkout you are in, then BITBUCKET\_PROJECT\_KEY + BITBUCKET\_REPO\_SLUG)

`--source-branch string`
:   Starting point branch

`--source-commit string`
:   Commit ID before editing

## `bb repo get`

Show a repository's details and its README

Aliases: `bb repo view`

```text
bb repo get [flags]
```

Show a repository's description, state and clone URLs, followed by its README.

The README is the file Bitbucket picks from the default branch, printed as raw markup: bb does not render it. A repository without a README says so rather than failing. --readme=false leaves the README out and skips the request for it.

bb repo view is the gh spelling of the same command. To open the repository in a browser, use bb browse.

```bash
# Describe a repository and print its README
bb repo get --repo PROJ/repo

# Only the details
bb repo get --repo PROJ/repo --readme=false
```

`--readme`
:   Include the README; --readme=false leaves it out (default true)

`--repo string`
:   Repository as PROJECT/slug (defaults to the repository of the git checkout you are in, then BITBUCKET\_PROJECT\_KEY + BITBUCKET\_REPO\_SLUG)

Also takes the [global flags](global-flags.md).

**Dry run:** Runs as usual: this command changes nothing, so there is nothing to hold back

<details class="note" data-search-exclude>
<summary>Output with <code>--json</code>, where <code>?</code> marks a field that can be absent</summary>
<pre><code>data
  repository        object
    id?             integer                                       Repository identifier.
    projectKey?     string                                        Project the repository belongs to.
    slug?           string                                        Repository slug, as it appears in URLs.
    name?           string                                        Display name, which may differ from the slug.
    description?    string                                        Description, when one was given.
    defaultBranch?  string                                        Branch a clone checks out, when the instance reports
                                                                  it.
    public          boolean                                       Whether the repository is readable without
                                                                  authentication.
    forkable        boolean                                       Whether users may fork it.
    archived        boolean                                       Whether it is archived and therefore read-only.
    scmId?          string                                        Source control system. git on every supported
                                                                  instance.
    state?          AVAILABLE|INITIALISING|INITIALISATION_FAILED
    statusMessage?  string                                        What the state means, when Bitbucket explains it.
    origin?         object                                        Repository this one was forked from.
      projectKey    string                                        Project key the repository belongs to.
      slug          string                                        Repository slug.
  cloneUrls         list of object or null                        Where the repository can be cloned from, one entry per
                                                                  protocol the instance serves.
    name            string                                        Protocol, as Bitbucket names it: http or ssh.
    url             string                                        The URL git clones from.
  readme?           object                                        The README.
    encoding        string                                        How content is encoded: utf-8 for text, base64 for
                                                                  anything that is not valid UTF-8.
    content         string                                        The README as raw markup.
</code></pre>

### `bb repo settings workflow`

Create, list and delete repository webhooks

#### `bb repo settings workflow webhooks`

Create, list and delete repository webhooks

#### `bb repo settings workflow webhooks create`

Create a repository webhook

```text
bb repo settings workflow webhooks create <name> <url> [flags]
```

```bash
# Call an endpoint when anything is pushed to the repository
bb repo settings workflow webhooks create ci https://ci.example.com/hooks/bitbucket \
  --repo PROJ/repo

# On pull request events, signed with a shared secret read from stdin
printf '%s' "$WEBHOOK_SECRET" | bb repo settings workflow webhooks create reviews \
  https://ci.example.com/hooks/reviews --repo PROJ/repo \
  --event pr:opened --event pr:merged --secret-stdin
```

`--active`
:   Whether the webhook is active (default true)

`--credentials-password-stdin`
:   Read the endpoint password from stdin (or set BB\_WEBHOOK\_PASSWORD)

`--credentials-username string`
:   Username Bitbucket authenticates to the endpoint with

`--event strings`
:   Webhook event(s) to subscribe to (default \[repo:refs\_changed\])

`--secret-stdin`
:   Read the shared secret from stdin (or set BB\_WEBHOOK\_SECRET)

`--ssl-verification string`
:   Whether Bitbucket verifies the endpoint's TLS certificate, left as the server has it when omitted (one of: true, false)

Inherited from [`bb repo settings`](#bb-repo-settings):

`--repo string`
:   Repository as PROJECT/slug (defaults to the repository of the git checkout you are in, then BITBUCKET\_PROJECT\_KEY + BITBUCKET\_REPO\_SLUG)

Also takes the [global flags](global-flags.md).

**Dry run:** Checks your permission and the current state this depends on, without changing anything (preconditions-checked)

    name?                     string          Webhook name.
    url?                      string          Endpoint Bitbucket posts to.
    active                    boolean         Whether the webhook currently fires.

## `bb repo ssh-key`

Add, list and remove the SSH access keys of a project or repository

[`add`](#bb-repo-ssh-key-add)
:   Add a project or repository SSH access key

[`list`](#bb-repo-ssh-key-list)
:   List project or repository SSH access keys

[`remove`](#bb-repo-ssh-key-remove)
:   Remove a project or repository SSH access key by ID

### `bb repo ssh-key add`

Add a project or repository SSH access key

```text
bb repo ssh-key add <key-file-or-text> [flags]
```

```bash
# Give a deploy key read access to one repository
bb repo ssh-key add deploy-key.pub --repo PROJ/repo --label "CI deploy key"

# Read and write access to every repository of a project
bb repo ssh-key add deploy-key.pub --project PROJ --permission read-write
```

`--label string`
:   Label/comment for the SSH key

`--permission string`
:   Permission level (one of: read-only, read-write) (default "read-only")

`--read-only`
:   Add as read-only access key

`--read-write`
:   Add as read-write access key

Inherited from [`bb repo ssh-key`](#bb-repo-ssh-key):

`--project string`
:   Project key for project-level SSH keys

`--repo string`
:   Repository reference (projectKey/repositorySlug) for repository-level SSH keys

Also takes the [global flags](global-flags.md).

## `bb repo sync`

Bring a fork up to date with its origin, and turn automatic syncing on or off

```text
bb repo sync [flags]
```

```bash
# Bring a fork's default branch up to date with the repository it was forked from
bb repo sync --repo SANDBOX/repo-experiment

# One branch, throwing away what the fork has that upstream lacks
bb repo sync --repo SANDBOX/repo-experiment --ref release/1.2 --action DISCARD
```

`--action string`
:   How to reconcile the ref (one of: MERGE, DISCARD, REBASE) (default "MERGE")

`--ref string`
:   Ref to synchronize (defaults to the repository default branch)

`--repo string`
:   Repository as PROJECT/slug (defaults to the repository of the git checkout you are in, then BITBUCKET\_PROJECT\_KEY + BITBUCKET\_REPO\_SLUG)

Also takes the [global flags](global-flags.md).

**Dry run:** Predicts the outcome from what it can read, without changing anything (predicted)

<summary>Output with <code>--json</code>, where <code>?</code> marks a field that can be absent</summary>
<pre><code>data
  status        string                Outcome of the command.
  repository    object
    projectKey  string                Project key the repository belongs to.
    slug        string                Repository slug.
  ref           string                Ref that was synchronised.
  action        MERGE|DISCARD|REBASE  How the ref was reconciled with upstream, which decides what happens to local
                                      commits.
</code></pre>
</details>

[`disable`](#bb-repo-sync-disable)
:   Disable automatic background synchronization

[`enable`](#bb-repo-sync-enable)
:   Enable automatic background synchronization

[`status`](#bb-repo-sync-status)
:   Query synchronization status, divergence, and settings

### `bb repo sync disable`

Disable automatic background synchronization

```text
bb repo sync disable
```
